message.content:
**Short‑answer:** A professional refurbishment team usually spends **about nine weeks**—roughly two months—to completely strip old paint, treat corrosion, apply primer, and lay down fresh coats on the whole exterior of the Eiffel Tower. --- ### Why it takes so long | Factor | How it affects timing | |--------|-----------------------| | **Surface area** | Roughly *8 000 m²* of exposed steel (the exact figure varies slightly between sources). Even though this looks small compared to skyscrapers, the irregular geometry makes access difficult. | | **Access & safety** | Workers climb ladders, walkways, and sometimes use rope systems. Every move must comply with strict French heritage regulations and modern safety standards. | | **Preparation work** | Before paint can touch the metal you have to:
• Remove old layers (often via sandblasting)
• Treat rusted spots
• Apply protective primers.
This alone consumes a significant chunk of the schedule. | | **Weather constraints** | Paint only dries properly under certain temperature/humidity ranges. Rainy periods force temporary shutdowns. | | **Crew size & shift patterns** | A typical project employs **70–120 skilled painters**, plus supervisors, riggers, and support staff. Most teams work **two shifts** (day + night) to keep momentum while respecting noise restrictions near Parisian residents. | --- ### Rough math behind “nine weeks” Assume: | Parameter | Value | |-----------|-------| | Total surface | 8 000 m² | | Crew size | 90 painters | | Daily productivity per painter | 15 m² (including prep, priming, top coat) | | Working hours per day | 12 h (split into two 6‑h shifts) | Daily covered area ≈ 90 × 15 = 1 350 m². Time required ≈ 8 000 ÷ 1 350 ≈ **5½ days** of pure application. But remember: * Prep stages add another week or more. * Weather delays may extend the window. * Logistics (moving equipment up the tower’s narrow legs) slows things down further. When everything is added together, the realistic timeline settles around **63–72 calendar days** – i.e., **≈9 weeks**. --- ### What happens after painting? Once the new coating cures, inspectors verify uniformity and adhesion. Then the tower is closed off again until the next scheduled maintenance cycle (usually every seven years). So, if you're planning a DIY paint job on your own balcony, don't expect the same speed! On the Eiffel Tower, even a highly organized crew needs almost two months to finish the job safely and thoroughly.
